title: How far can you dilute?
hook: Dilute a dye by 1:10, again and again. When does the dye run out?

doesNotKnow: that a molecule count runs out, so dilution has an end

misconception: You can dilute forever and still have the stuff, only weaker.
objective: The learner can say that 10 mL of 1.0 mol/L dye holds about 6.0 × 10²¹ molecules, so after about 22 tenfold steps the average tube holds fewer than 1.

claims.text: The Avogadro constant is 6.02214076 × 10²³ per mole.
10 mL of 1.0 mol/L dye holds about 6.0 × 10²¹ molecules.
claims.source: 1.0 mol/L x 0.010 L x 6.02214e23 = 6.022e21 (node; Demo.tsx stock).

claims.text: After k 1:10 steps the 10 mL tube holds on average 6.0 × 10²¹ × 10^-k molecules: about 6.0 at step 21 and about 0.60 at step 22.
claims.source: 6.022e21 x 10^-21 = 6.022; 6.022e21 x 10^-22 = 0.6022 (node; Demo.tsx average()). Each step moves 1 mL of the previous tube into 9 mL of water.

claims.text: The number in any one tube is random: at an average of 0.60 about 55% of tubes hold none and the rest hold one or more.
claims.source: Poisson distribution: P(0) = exp(-0.6022) = 0.547 (node). Assumes molecules are well mixed and independent.

claims.text: The sample tube drawn from step 19 on uses a fixed seed (3000 + step), chosen from six tried because it shows 5 molecules at step 21 and 0 at step 22; it illustrates a typical outcome, not a guarantee.
claims.source: Demo.tsx sample(); seed bases 1000 to 7000 gave 5 to 11 at step 21 and 0 or 1 at step 22 (node).

claims.text: The model assumes ideal mixing and no loss of molecules to the walls; real tubes also adsorb some dye.
claims.source: Stage chip 'Each step: 1 mL into 9 mL water. Tube = 10 mL.' and this claim; adsorption is a standard caveat of serial dilution.

claims.text: From step 19 the stage also draws 20 seeded sample tubes (seeds 3000 + step + 1301 x draw number, draws 1 to 20) and says how many hold none (12 of 20 at step 22); the reveal quotes that count and says another 20 would differ a little. The multiplier 1301 was chosen from fourteen tried so the run sits near the 55% average; this is one fixed illustration, not a measurement.
claims.source: Poisson sampler in Demo.tsx emptyOf(k): count of zero results among 20 seeded draws (builder node run: multiplier 1301 gives 0 empty at step 21 and 12 at step 22; the earlier multiplier 977 gave 15, a tail draw). Expected 20 x 0.547 = 10.9. Chosen-seed disclosure as in c5.

recall.question: A tube holds 6 × 10⁶ molecules on average. You dilute it 1:10 repeatedly. After how many steps does the average first drop below 1?
recall.why: 6 × 10⁶ x 10^-6 = 6, which is still above 1; 6 × 10⁶ x 10^-7 = 0.6, which is below 1. So 7 steps.
